children: U.S. jobless claims pulled back slightly but were largely unchanged as the labor market holds steady.

The number of people who filed for unemployment benefits was 206,000 in the week through Sept. 5, 1,000 lower than the upwardly revised 207,000 reported a week earlier, the Labor Department said Thursday. Economists surveyed by The Wall Street Journal were expecting to see the figure come in at 205,000.

Continuing claims, which scale with the total size of the unemployed population, totaled just over 1.77 million in the week through August 29, sliding by just 1,000 from the downwardly revised total a week earlier. The data on continuing claims lag the initial-claims data by a week.
The Conference Board said earlier this week that it was seeing signs that underemployment is easing, and that perceptions of job availability are improving.
